# `non-exhaustive-error-switch`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports a switch over a known finite error set that does not name every error.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Exhaustive error handling makes newly introduced failures visible instead of
routing them through an accidental fallback.

## When it fires

It applies when the operand's error set is explicitly known; inferred or global
error sets are not expanded speculatively.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const E = error{ A, B, C };

fn f(e: E) u32 {
    return switch (e) {
        error.A => 1,
        error.B => 2,
    };
}
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/#Exhaustive-Switching>
